sara: quick heads-up — ran a perfetto trace on a mixed workload (short chat + occasional long completion). seeing repeating HBM bandwidth dips aligned with KV cache evictions, roughly every ~600ms. trace: https://perfetto.link/xyz123 :warning:
jonah: got the link, can you paste the nsys timeline snippet or nvprof summary?
sara: pasted the important slice below (nsys timeline):
```
# nsys slice (reduced)
Time(ms)    Kernel            SM Util   DRAM BW(GB/s)   Notes
1200-1220   mha_attn_v2       82%       220            burst during long seq
1220-1226   kv_read_pages     15%       5              eviction scan, big memcpy
1226-1800   idle/overlap      20%       40             periodic thrash until next long seq
```
kev: that kv_read_pages line at low SM util but causing DRAM stalls looks like read amplification from the per-request window scanner. are we scanning whole KV slab instead of a windowed lookup?
sara: yes — heuristic currently falls back to full-scan when seqlen > 2048 and batch mix > 0.2. repro steps in trace: send 3 short (64) + 1 long (4096) then storm.
natalie: hmm. could be interacting with batching heuristics: microbatch sizes jump to keep latency for short requests but that increases concurrent KV walkers and causes HBM contention.
jonah: quick experiment idea: disable the long-seq fallback scan and use probabilistic index (sampled bloom) for long reads, or throttle concurrent KV walkers. can we try a runtime flag?
sara: will try flag now: `INFER_KV_SCAN=prob-sample INFER_MAX_CONCUR_KV=2` and re-run the same mixed workload. will share new perfetto link in ~10m.
perf-bot: deploy detected: infra/kv-cache-heuristic toggled for canary (user=sara).
sara: first quick run looks promising — DRAM BW max drops and troughs smooth out, no big memcpy spikes. short-term mitigation verified. attaching new trace: https://perfetto.link/xyz124
jonah: nice. can you also run a kernel selection trace? suspect kernel churn: scheduler picks different attention kernel for long seq and that increases memory pressure due to temporary allocations.
sara: ran kernel-selection debug log: `kernel_choice: mha_attn_v2 -> mha_attn_large_seq_quant` whenever long starts; fallback to v2 for short ones. churn frequency ~0.9/sec.
kev: if kernel churn correlates with microbatch switch, maybe keep kernel pinned per-device for N seconds or until KV window stabilized. cheap rule: don't switch kernels more than once per 1s per-stream.
natalie: we'll want an A/B: (A) throttled KV walkers + kernel pin window, (B) probabilistic scan only. measure p99 latency and tokens/sec and HBM 95th pct.
sara: agreed. running A/B now on 2 nodes. initial numbers: A reduces HBM 95p by ~38%, p99 latency up 4% for long seqs. B reduces HBM 95p by ~22%, p99 down 2% on short seqs but long seq throughput worse.
jonah: good signal. plan: ship quick mitigation (throttle KV walkers + pin kernel for 1.2s) to canary, add sampled index option as follow-up. will open a PR.
sara: created draft PR: https://git.redwood/infra/kv-heuristics/pulls/321 — includes config, a small unit test, and updated profiling notes.
kev: add a perf regression test: synthetic mixed workload with 1:3 long:short, assert HBM 95p < 120GB/s and no memcpy burst > 1.2s.
natalie: also add an eval hook to catch drift: if kernel churn > 0.5/s, alert to eng-runtime.
jonah: +1. thanks team — great triage loop. follow-up meeting in #eng-runtime sync tomorrow to decide on default rollout. :thumbsup:
